sentences.text: The petitioners were doing business on the said property under the name and style of "Toys Centre" for commercial purposes in which they were dealing in sale and purchase of new cycles and their parts.
Both the shops have class 'A' construction and were fully renovated with wood work, marble work etc.
Further, other than petitioners, no other person has any right, title or interest in the shops and only petitioners are entitled to compensation/ enhanced compensation.
The petitioners are not satisfied with the compensation amount awarded by the LAC, determination of market value of land in question, measurement of land etc.

ii. The LAC has mistakenly assessed the market value of land and structures of petitioners at low rates which does not represents the market value of the land on the date of notification U/s 4 of LA, Act.

iii. The LAC has wrongly assessed the market value of land in question @ Rs.2805/-
per sq.mt. whereas as on the date of notification U/s 4, L.A. Act, the market value of the shops was much more than Rs.50,00,000/-.
The market value of the land alone was more than Rs.2,00,000/-.

iv. The LAC has failed to consider that the property in question us a built up commercial property located on Main Bazaar Road, Railway Road, Shahdara, which is prestigious and famous market and no land is available for sale in this area and in its vicinity at any price.

All facilities and amenities like electricity, water, mettled road, banks, Railway Station etc. were available prior to the date of notification U/s 4, L.A. Act.
v.
The LAC has further failed to consider the sale rates of commercial properties in the vicinity.
Even the sale consideration of properties sold by DDA and other agencies has not been considered.

vi. In addition, LAC has failed to appreciate that land in question and the super structure were situated in the main market, Railway Road, Shahdara and surrounded by fully developed market from all sides.
All the amenities like electricity, mettled road, water, sewage, railway station, banks highway etc. were available prior to the date of notification U/s 4, L.A. Act.
Even Shahdara Railway Station is about 15-20 sq.yds. away from the acquired land.
Banks, NH no.1, cinema halls, hospitals, Old Shahdara Court etc. were also situated near the acquired LAC No.40/16 Sh. Om Prakash Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 4 of 13 land.

sentences.text: a) Onus to prove this issue is upon the petitioners.

By virtue of this reference, the petitioners are seeking enhancement in compensation in respect of compulsory acquisition of their Shop No.1/1145,
First Floor and construction on Second Floor measuring 16.72 square meters on account of acquired land beneath the shop, shifting charges of business, construction cost including furnitures and fixtures, damages on account of change in place of business including business goodwill.

However,
during the course of arguments, certified copy of the judgment passed in reference petition U/s 30-31, L.A. Act was placed on record wherein the claim of the petitioners was declined on account of land compensation for Shop bearing no.1/1145 (First Floor), situated at Main Bazar, Railway Road,
Shahdara, Khasra No.446 min, Village Chandrawali, Shahdara as petitioners neither having any right, title or interest in the land beneath the shop in question nor their names figured in the list of recorded owners in the award and their names have been figured only for the compensation for the structure which has already been granted to them.
The said judgment has attained finality as not challenged by either party till date, as per record.
The relevant para of the judgment is reproduced herein:-

"In view of my findings on issue no.1, IPs no.396 are not entitled to land compensation for shop bearing no. 1/1145 (First Floor) measuring LAC No.40/16 Sh.
Om Prakash Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 10 of 13 15.20 sq. metres and another shop no. 1/1144 (First Floor) measuring about 16.72 sq. metres, both situated at Main Bazar, Railway Road, Shahdara, comprised in Khasra No.446 min of revenue estate of Village Chandrawali, Shahdara, Delhi".
b) In view of the findings of the Reference Court U/s 30-31, L.A. Act, it is held

sentences.text:
that since no share in land has been granted in favour of the petitioners in respect of shop bearing no.1/1145 (First Floor),
situated at Main Bazar, Railway Road, Shahdara, Khasra No.446 min, Village Chandrawali,
Shahdara, they were not entitled to any compensation qua the land acquired vide Award No.01/1999-2000.

Further as far as claim qua loss of goodwill and shifting charges are concerned,
since no evidence has been led in this regard, the petitioners are not entitled for any compensation on this aspect.
Further, as per record a sum of Rs.89,000/- has already been granted in favour of the petitioners in respect of the super structure there upon.

Though, petitioners claim that they suffered huge losses on account of demolition of the structure over the land acquired in question, however,
apart from mere bald submissions, no evidence has been led in this regard.

Rather on the contrary,
the valuation report Ex.PW1/1 placed on record by the petitioner himself, shows the total cost of construction of the structure in question at Rs.1,01,000/-.
Accordingly, the compensation awarded to the tune of Rs.89,000/- towards the structural cost is sufficient and thus do not warrant any interference from this Court.
Hence, this issue is decided against the petitioners.

a) The onus to prove this issue is upon the petitioners.

However, apart from mere bald averments,
neither any evidence has been led nor argued in this regard.
The proviso to Section 18 of L.A. Act provides for period of limitation during which an application for reference to the Court can be made to the Collector.

The same reads as under:-
"Section 18. Reference to Court:-
(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the persons to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made.
(a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collector's award.

(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12, sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collector's award, which period shall first expire".
b) Though no evidence has been led to prove this issue, however, on perusal of record, it is observed that in the instant case, award was pronounced on 20.07.1999 whereas petitioners have preferred their claim petition u/s 18 of L.A Act before LAC on 30.08.1999 as per the diary entry vide No.26/LAC (Shahdara)/30.08.1999 as mentioned on the copy of reference petition sent to this court u/s 18 of L.A Act by the LAC.
Meaning thereby, it has been filed within six weeks from the date of award LAC No.40/16 Sh. Om Prakash Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 12 of 13 and thus, within limitation.

sentences.text: Even otherwise, nothing substantial is brought on record on behalf of the respondents to show how the present reference is barred by limitation.
Even in the written submissions filed on behalf of respondents, no objection as to the limitation has been taken.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioners.

the valuation report Ex.PW1/1 placed on record by the petitioner himself, shows the total cost of construction of the structure in question at Rs.1,01,000/-.

Meaning thereby, it has been filed within six weeks from the date of award LAC No.40/16 Sh. Om Prakash Vs. Union of India & Anr. Pg No. 12 of 13 and thus, within limitation.
Even otherwise, nothing substantial is brought on record on behalf of the respondents to show how the present reference is barred by limitation.
